title: AI-enhanced surgical planning and possibly AI-designed skull implants in the Abu Dhabi separation of craniopagus twins Mercy and Goodness
summary: PureHealth/SKMC statement (5 June 2026) cites “AI-enhanced surgical planning”; XRlabs' own release claims AI-designed implants. The twins were separated in four operations and returned to Nigeria.
account: The Abu Dhabi Media Office published PureHealth's statement on 5 June 2026. Sheikh Khalifa Medical City (SKMC) had performed the GCC's first separation of craniopagus twins. Mercy and Goodness were born in Nigeria with “heads joined at the top, fused skulls, and intertwined brain tissue and blood vessels”. They were separated at 15 months in four procedures over six months. The team was “more than 60 doctors and clinicians from the UAE, UK, Brazil, and Nigeria”. Professor Noor Ul Owase Jeelani of Gemini Untwined led the work. The statement lists “mixed reality-guided implant design and AI-enhanced surgical planning” among the methods and names no software. It says the skulls were reconstructed with custom 3D-printed titanium grafts and the twins were recovering well. The National and Khaleej Times (both 5 June 2026) report the same facts without the words AI or artificial intelligence. A CNN report carried by WKRC (22 June 2026) says the teams “used artificial intelligence, mixed reality and virtual simulations to map out the procedures”. It says AI “helped surgeons design custom skull implants and model how the girls” skin could be expanded'. It says the four surgeries totaled over 40 hours across four months in 2025, with the twins since home in Nigeria. The only system-specific claim is XRlabs' own Business Wire release of 19 June 2026, read via Medical Product Outsourcing. It says its platform let surgeons “design implants within seconds” from computed tomography (CT) data in mixed reality. It used an AI model “trained on similarly aged infant head shapes”. No case report of these twins has been found in Europe PMC. It noted that the surgical group's 2026 Radiology paper on craniopagus imaging does not mention AI. The surgery dates are not published.
purpose: XRlabs says its platform is built to design patient-specific implants and plan operations in mixed reality. The hospital's “AI-enhanced surgical planning” is described only generically. Implant design for this separation was the vendor's stated purpose.
system: XRlabs 'Surgical Intelligence' platform for AI-designed skull implants (identified only by the vendor) and unnamed 'AI-enhanced surgical planning' (PureHealth statement)
developer: XRlabs (implant design, per its own release); the hospital names no developer for the planning tools
deployer: PureHealth - SEHA Sheikh Khalifa Medical City, Abu Dhabi, with Gemini Untwined (Professor Noor Ul Owase Jeelani)
domain: Healthcare - pediatric neurosurgery and craniofacial surgery
segment: Craniopagus twin separation: surgical planning and patient-specific implants
taxonomy_note: The AI's claimed part is surgical planning; the good recorded is the twins' separation.

ratings.reason: Two children joined at the head were separated, reconstructed and discharged home to Nigeria, per the hospital and press. The surgical team produced this outcome, and no source quantifies the AI's share of it.
The vendor claims implant design “within seconds”, and CNN reports the fastest of nine Gemini Untwined separations. No source gives planning time saved or a comparison without the AI.

ai_role.statement: The hospital's own statement credits “AI-enhanced surgical planning” without naming a system. CNN says AI helped design the skull implants and model skin expansion. People/AOL attributes AI vaguely to skin-expander timing. The only identification of a system is XRlabs' own release, which cites no clinical publication. The AI supported planning and implant design for a 60-person team. No counterfactual is given, and the separation itself was surgical work.

later.quote: Doctors reported the surgeries were successful, and the girls have since returned home to Nigeria after making a full recovery.
